# SlopStopper

> A Python CLI plus GitHub Actions workflows that run security, hygiene and
> reliability checks on every PR. One command to install into any repo.
> Stops AI-generated "slop" reaching production; humans, agents and CI all
> invoke every check through one `task ss:*` surface.

SlopStopper is two things at once: a portable quality suite you install into
your own repo via `install.sh`, and a live reference site (this one) built and
deployed with the same suite it advertises.

## Site

- [Home](https://slopstopper.dev/): what SlopStopper is and how to get started
- [Features](https://slopstopper.dev/features.html): the five loops (security, hygiene, reliability and operational are installed; deployment shows how this site ships, to copy) and every check
- [Tools](https://slopstopper.dev/tools.html): the underlying kit: Semgrep, OWASP ZAP, Trivy, Gitleaks, Playwright, axe-core, Lighthouse CI, GitHub Actions, Task
- [Learn](https://slopstopper.dev/learn.html): the course, twenty-one short lessons, each check explained and run against a demo repo the CLI writes; each lesson is a page under /learn/, listed below
- [Docs](https://slopstopper.dev/docs.html): the reference docs rendered as pages under /docs/, listed below: every check's rules, knobs and report, adopting the suite, the architecture, the runbooks and the change map
- [Feedback](https://slopstopper.dev/feedback.html): report a bug or request a check
- [Privacy](https://slopstopper.dev/privacy.html): what the site collects (nothing of its own), what Cloudflare keeps as the host, and which other services the pages reach

## The course

One lesson per page, in order; each one's goal is its summary.

<!-- learn:begin -->
- [Lesson 0: What slop is, and the five loops](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/00-what-slop-is.html): Say what slopstopper stops and how, so every later lesson has a frame to sit in.
- [Lesson 1: Install slopstopper into a repo](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/01-install.html): Install the suite into a repo, pick a profile, know what every file it wrote is for, and see which checks the repo is now carrying.
- [Lesson 2: Run your first check and read its report](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/02-first-check-complexity.html): Run one check against the demo repo, read the red line and the report it points at, fix what it names, and see it go green. This is the loop every later lesson repeats.
- [Lesson 3: Entry files: the AGENTS.md-first model](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/03-entry-files.html): Say why README.md and AGENTS.md have token budgets, find the demo's README over its budget, and see that the fix is to move content deeper and route it, never to raise the budget.
- [Lesson 4: Docs structure: every doc has a route](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/04-docs-structure.html): Find the doc in the demo that nothing routes to, see why a "see also" link does not count, route it, and understand the hop and line limits.
- [Lesson 5: Docs accuracy and docs size](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/05-docs-accuracy-and-size.html): Find the doc in the demo that describes a command the repo does not have, read the finding, make the doc true, and then read the growth signal the size monitor prints without ever failing a build.
- [Lesson 6: Secrets](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/06-secrets.html): Commit a fake private key to the demo, watch Gitleaks catch it, see why deleting it in a later commit does not help, and learn the fix that does.
- [Lesson 7: Static analysis](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/07-sast.html): Find the one unsafe line in the demo's script, read the finding Semgrep raised for it, and fix the code rather than the rule.
- [Lesson 8: Dependencies and licences](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/08-dependencies.html): Find the pinned package in the demo with a known CVE, read the report's "Fixed In" column, take the fix, and see where the licence gates sit.
- [Lesson 9: Headers and CSP](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/09-headers-and-csp.html): See the headers the demo's host sends, find the Content-Security-Policy relaxation nobody wrote down, document it properly, and then audit an API's CORS headers and fix the commonest mistake.
- [Lesson 10: Dynamic scanning](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/10-dast.html): Serve the demo, run OWASP ZAP against it, read a baseline report, see what the gate accepts and why, and accept one finding with a reason.
- [Lesson 11: Smoke and end-to-end](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/11-smoke-and-e2e.html): Serve the demo, run the two browser checks that prove it works for a visitor, break each one the way a real change would, and read what the browser saw.
- [Lesson 12: Accessibility](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/12-accessibility.html): Audit both of the demo's pages with axe-core, find the one attribute a screen reader depends on that the history page is missing, and fix it.
- [Lesson 13: Core Web Vitals](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/13-core-web-vitals.html): Run Lighthouse against the demo, read the budget it enforces, add one blocking script, and watch the numbers move.
- [Lesson 14: SEO and social share](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/14-seo.html): Audit the tags a search engine and a link preview read, find the one the demo's history page is missing, and see which surface it would have broken.
- [Lesson 15: Discoverability: robots, sitemap, llms.txt and links](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/15-discoverability.html): Run the four checks that decide whether anyone finds a page, fix the one the demo ships red, and break the other three to see which catches what.
- [Lesson 16: API checks: health, latency and OpenAPI drift](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/16-api-checks.html): Point the three API checks at a small API, see each one fail on its own kind of drift, and understand why they exist alongside the browser checks.
- [Lesson 17: CI: the workflows and the PR feedback loop](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/17-ci.html): Read one check workflow end to end, see that it is the same task line you have been typing, and follow a red check from the Actions log to the pull request comment to the issue it raises on main.
- [Lesson 18: Agents: the install and triage skills](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/18-agents.html): Install the two Claude Code skills into a repo, read how they are shaped, and see how an agent uses them to install the suite or fix a red check without being told the steps.
- [Lesson 19: Profiles and tailoring](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/19-profiles-and-tailoring.html): Switch a repo between the ui, api and library profiles, keep one check a profile drops, and know where the CLI pin lives and how it moves.
- [Lesson 20: Inside slopstopper: add a check](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/20-inside-slopstopper.html): Register a new check in the CLI, let the test suite tell you the other surfaces it must be wired into, and understand the shape every check shares.
<!-- learn:end -->

## Docs

One page per reference doc, by section; each section's index says when to read what.

<!-- docs:begin -->
- [Docs index](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/index.html): The fallback routing table (a README so it renders in place when you browse docs/). AGENTS.md carries what most tasks need and routes the common cases directly; come here when your task is not covered there. Read only the doc whose trigger matches. Each row says when, and each category README…
- [Runbooks: Runbooks](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/runbooks/index.html): Operational procedures for the SlopStopper project, covering both the suite itself and the things adopters do once around it.
- [Runbooks: Adopting SlopStopper](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/runbooks/install.html): Everything an adopter needs once: prerequisites, what the installer writes, what each check needs from you, how to run the suite, configure it and move the CLI pin. The README holds the two install commands; this is the rest.
- [Runbooks: Install the SlopStopper Claude Code skills](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/runbooks/install-skills.html): The companion to install.sh. Where install.sh drops the whole quality suite into a repo, install-skill.sh targets just the Claude Code skill subset, which is useful for refreshing the playbooks without re-running the full installer.
- [Runbooks: Cutting a release](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/runbooks/release.html): slopstopper-cli releases are automated end-to-end via two GitHub workflows:
- [Runbooks: Upgrade the pinned slopstopper-cli](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/runbooks/upgrade-cli.html): slopstopper-cli is pinned per-repo. The pin lives in mise.toml as the [tools] entry "pipx:slopstopper-cli", and mise installs it both locally and in CI (via jdx/mise-action). mise activates the tool per-directory, so the active slopstopper always matches the repo you're in and there's no single…
- [Hygiene: Hygiene](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/hygiene/index.html): Overview of code and documentation hygiene and quality gates.
- [Hygiene: Agentic Documentation Updater](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/hygiene/doc-updater.html): The repo ships a weekly agentic workflow that scans recently-merged PRs, identifies documentation drift, and opens a sync PR with the proposed fixes. It runs on GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw) with the GitHub Copilot CLI engine.
- [Security: Security](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/index.html): Security scanning and controls for this project: what each security: check looks at, how it blocks, and where to tune it. One file per check; this page is the map, so read only the doc whose trigger matches.
- [Security: API Headers & CORS](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/api-headers.html): The API-shaped analogue of CSP Exceptions. On an HTML surface, CSP is the header that decides what a document may load. On a JSON API there is no document to restrict, so CSP is largely irrelevant and CORS becomes the control that decides who may read the response. A permissive CORS policy on a…
- [Security: CSP exceptions](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/csp-exceptions.html): This file is the single source of truth for every per-path Content-Security-Policy relaxation on the SlopStopper site. The ss:hygiene:csp-exceptions check fails the build if worker/headers.json and this file disagree.
- [Security: Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST)](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/dast.html): This template includes automated Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) using OWASP ZAP to detect runtime security issues by scanning your running site. This guide explains how to customise and use this feature.
- [Security: Licence Inventory](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/licences.html): security:licences judges every dependency the lockfiles resolve to against the repo's licence allowlist, so a transitive package under a denied licence cannot sit in the tree unnoticed. It is the full-tree companion to the dependency review, which judges only what each PR adds.
- [Security: Static Application Security Testing (SAST)](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/sast.html): This template includes automated Static Application Security Testing (SAST) using Semgrep to detect security bugs and anti-patterns in your own source code. This guide explains how to customise and use this feature.
- [Security: Secrets Detection](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/secrets.html): This template includes automated secrets detection using Gitleaks to identify hardcoded credentials, API keys, and other sensitive data in your source code and git history. This guide explains how to customise and use this feature.
- [Security: Dependency Vulnerability Scanning](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/vulnerability.html): This template includes automated dependency vulnerability scanning using Trivy to detect known CVEs in your project's dependencies. This guide explains how to customise and use this feature.
- [Reliability: Reliability Testing](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/index.html): SlopStopper's reliability checks, wired against any reachable URL: portable smoke tests, broken-link audits, and the API health and latency audits (all below), plus seven audits with their own guide. Read the one whose trigger matches.
- [Reliability: Accessibility Monitoring](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/accessibility.html): This directory documents automated accessibility monitoring for the site. Accessibility is audited on every pull request, push to main, successful deployment, and on a daily schedule.
- [Reliability: Core Web Vitals](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/cwv.html): reliability:cwv runs Lighthouse CI against a URL and fails the build when a page's performance falls below budget. It is the browser-side speed check; API Latency is its analogue for a JSON API.
- [Reliability: E2E Journeys](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/e2e.html): Smoke proves each page renders. The E2E check proves a visitor can get around: it drives a browser through the journeys any HTML site offers, without knowing anything about yours. From every start path the bundled Playwright spec:
- [Reliability: llms.txt AI-Discoverability Check](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/llms-txt.html): ss:reliability:llms-txt, implemented in cli/slopstopper/checks/llms_txt.py, audits your site's /llms.txt as the llmstxt.org convention defines it. llms.txt is a curated markdown map at the site root that lets AI assistants and agents read your key content directly, instead of parsing noisy HTML.…
- [Reliability: robots.txt Discoverability Check](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/robots-txt.html): ss:reliability:robots-txt, implemented in cli/slopstopper/checks/robots_txt.py, audits your site's /robots.txt, which is the Robots Exclusion Protocol file every crawler reads first. Its headline job is the de-index guard: a stray Disallow: / under User-agent:  (often leaked from a staging…
- [Reliability: SEO & Social-Share Metatag Check](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/seo.html): SlopStopper ships two complementary SEO-flavoured checks:
- [Reliability: sitemap.xml Completeness + Drift Check](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/sitemap.html): ss:reliability:sitemap, implemented in cli/slopstopper/checks/sitemap.py, crawls your site from / and cross-checks the served sitemap.xml against the pages it actually reaches. Where ss:reliability:llms-txt and ss:reliability:robots-txt assert those files exist and are well-formed, this check…
- [Architecture: Architecture](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/architecture/index.html): Architecture structure and boundaries overview for this static site hosted on a Cloudflare Worker.
- [Architecture: PR feedback: one summary, compact detail](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/architecture/pr-feedback.html): Every check writes a standalone report with an H1, an overall verdict, per-item sections, folded evidence and a "How to Fix" section. That is the right shape for a file you open deliberately. It is the wrong shape for nineteen of them stacked on a pull request, which is what posting each report…
- [Architecture: Project-shape profiles](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/architecture/profiles.html): Not every check applies to every repo. The nine browser-and-SEO reliability checks (smoke, E2E, accessibility, Core Web Vitals, SEO, broken links, llms.txt, robots.txt, sitemap) assume HTML, a DOM and a public web surface. On an HTTP API they don't quietly no-op. They build, serve and audit…
- [Architecture: slopstopper-steward: the org-wide operator](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/architecture/steward.html): slopstopper is per-repo: it tells one repo what is wrong and ships how to fix it. hungovercoders/slopstopper-steward is the counterpart that works across an organisation. On a schedule it finds every repo with slopstopper installed, moves CLI pins that fell behind, and works the issues…
- [Deployment: Deployment](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/deployment/index.html): How the SlopStopper site ships to production.
- [The site: App](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/app/index.html): What the site does and how its pages are organised.
- [Contributing: Contributing](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/contributing/index.html): This document defines the default way to contribute to this project.
- [Contributing: Change map: every surface a change must touch](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/contributing/change-map.html): SlopStopper is a suite adopters install and a site that proves it works, so one change usually lands in several places: the CLI, a workflow, the installer, the config schema, the docs, the two Claude Code skills and the site copy. This table is the checklist; cli/tests/test_check_registration.py…
- [Contributing: Demo recordings](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/contributing/demos.html): The GIF in README.md and the stills beside it are recorded from the real CLI with VHS, from the tapes under demos/, and live next to them. They are committed, so a reader never needs the tooling; a contributor re-records when what a command prints changes.
- [Contributing: The demo repo](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/contributing/fixture.html): slopstopper demo writes a small fixture repository, shipped in the CLI wheel under cli/slopstopper/data/demo/, for anything that needs a repo to run slopstopper against with no network and no clone of this one: the course, the demo tapes, a triage walkthrough, the skill evals. It is "Lantern", a…
- [Contributing: Common pitfalls when extending SlopStopper](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/contributing/pitfalls.html): A short list of the most-hit gotchas. Each one has bitten somebody before; the rule is "do the obvious thing the obvious way."
- [Decisions: Decisions](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/decisions/index.html): This directory records significant decisions and their rationale for the project.
- [Support: Support](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/support/index.html): How to get help with this project.
- [The course: From zero to slopstopper](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/learn/index.html): A course in twenty-one short lessons, each with a YouTube episode to follow. You start with nothing installed and finish able to install the suite into a repo, read any check's red line and the report it points at, fix what it found, tailor the suite to a repo's shape, and add a check of your…
- [The course: Episode conventions](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/learn/episodes.html): The YouTube title, thumbnail and description conventions for the "From zero to slopstopper" series, and the recording notes every episode follows, so the series reads as one thing. Each lesson's own script is the collapsed "Episode script" at the end of its page; this file is what those scripts…
- [The course: Writing a lesson](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/learn/template.html): This page is the template every lesson in the course is copied from, and the rules a lesson follows. Copy it to docs/learn/<NN>-<slug>.md, keep the H1 as Lesson N: <title>, replace each section, and update the row in the syllabus.

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper): source, install.sh and the slopstopper CLI
- [README](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper/blob/main/README.md): install and usage
- [Documentation map](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/index.html): the routing table for every doc, as agents read it in the repo
- [From zero to slopstopper](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/learn/index.html): the course's syllabus and lesson sources, with an episode to follow
- [Agent guide](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper/blob/main/AGENTS.md): what most tasks in the repo need, within ~2k tokens

## For agents

- [slopstopper-install skill](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper/blob/main/.claude/skills/slopstopper-install/SKILL.md): install SlopStopper into a repo or refresh an existing install
- [slopstopper-triage skill](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper/blob/main/.claude/skills/slopstopper-triage/SKILL.md): diagnose and fix a failing SlopStopper check
- [slopstopper-steward](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper-steward): across a GitHub organisation, upgrades every adopter and works the issues the suite raised, one PR each. Each organisation runs its own fork or template copy; [its setup runbook](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper-steward/blob/main/docs/runbooks/SETUP.md) walks the copy, the GitHub App and the first dry run
